title: Logspace recognition of the valid-code language
statement: For every finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean input and work-tape symbols, the language consisting of encodings of pairs $(x,	ext{code}(c,s))$ for which $c$ is the configuration code of an $N$-configuration on input $x$ whose work-tape heads and nonblank cells lie within distance $s$ of the origin is decidable in logarithmic space. Here the encoding uses the self-delimiting pair encoding described above, and the configuration code is the binary value of the prescribed configuration word.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols
